notes.title: Development Update
notes.content:
To prepare for more building and exploration features, work has already begun on the overhaul of the world map screen in Grabbus!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45521474/34d598cefc69eb4a47349e8b3fc03fc5aea75aa3.png[/img]

In Grabbus, the world is generated on-the-fly using procedural "cloudy" noise to determine the default appearance and height of a tile.

The output of two of these layers of noise is used as a coordinate on a 2d graph of biomes that can be assigned to any given tile.

These biomes relate to the terrain-generation rules and coloration of a tile.
There are 9 "points" on the current biome graph that are blended between, so that transitions between biomes appear more gradual and smooth.

The plan for this overhaul is:
[list]
[*] -Cut the usage of the expensive re-coloring shader, allowing for more performance headroom.
[*] -Go from 9 biomes to [b]16[/b]
[*] -Give each biome its own set of ground tiles that are meant to look nice next to its neighboring biomes, making each area more distinct and colorful, which opens up certain gameplay possibilities later...
[*] -Adjust the terrain generation rules to match with the newly-added biomes
[*] -Give each tile sprite a set of variations to help break up repeating patterns
[*] -Increase the pixel size of tiles, allowing the map to better fill the screen and make it easier to use/see
[*] -Add a "sky" effect layer for the background
[*] -Add a shading layer for a day/night cycle
[/list]

We are VERY excited to get this big change to the world map implemented, since that will make way for more gameplay systems that can take advantage of there being specific things to find in specific areas.

This is just one of many big new features on its way, so please look forward to more updates as the art and programming catches up to the vision!

notes.title: GRABBUS - Patch Notes v0.2.3
notes.content:
[list]
[*] -Recipes involving containers fused with non-container items were pointing to the wrong code, resulting in the wrong potency values, these fusion recipes should now work as intended
[*] -Enemy and Treasure Orb spawn rate both slightly increased
[*] -Bonus fusion sparks awarded for completing a floor at full health has been reduced slightly, and will also trigger upon beating the final floor regardless of amount of health left, as opposed to dropping HP orbs which would be useless at that point.
[*] -The inventory can no longer be opened during a camera-move, and will automatically be closed if one is initiated
[*] -The strength of an enemy's weapon now contributes far less reward-value to their loot, and this reward value is also less effective at increasing rarity of enemy loot
[*] -When applying rarity to a newly-dropped weapon, any elixir infusions that are part of the internal rarity-granting process are drastically less powerful
[*] -Enemies are now less likely to drop elixirs
[*] -Boosting effect of the "Cache Attractor" relic has been greatly reduced
[*] -Projectiles will no longer reduce their size too far below the usual minimum as a result of splitting or other shot events
[*] -The final two enemies remaining per floor will no longer be able to enter the "escape-to-heal" behavior state.
[*] -Healing elixirs, when consumed, are now less than half as effective as before 
[/list]

notes.title: GRABBUS - Patch Notes v0.2.2
notes.content:
Today's patch focuses on some of the smaller, quicker fixes that could be addressed.
We are interested in seeing how this affects the feeling of balance! That sweet spot will take some adjustment to find, but hopefully, these changes can get us closer.

[list]
[*] -Screen shake can now be toggled on or off
[*] -The explosion elixir no longer affects environment tiles
[*] -The method used to generate random rolls to determine an "extra number" of times to drop items or trigger other effects has been adjusted
[*] -The potency-granting elixir gives less power to weapons fused with it, and now drains faster and less efficiently the higher its potency is
[*] -Dungeon size has been adjusted to start slightly larger, but scale a bit less with difficulty
[*] -Decay time of quantagon pickups has been extended
[*] -Items now take potency damage when striking anything after being thrown
[*] -Enemies now take more base damage when striking anything after being thrown
[*] -Remaining enemy HP is now factored in to the total damage done by having something thrown [b]at[/b] that enemy
[*] -Enemy stun countdown is now slowed to half speed while an enemy is grabbed
[*] -Morris now takes damage from falling off the stage
[*] -The camera will now prioritize Morris over the rainbow seed while he's holding up the cycle fuel
[/list]

notes.title: Roadmap!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45521474/bffd4409d59ea134cd5f470a077ad573ce0631d1.png[/img]

[h1][b]Immediate:[/b][/h1]
[h3][i]-Feedback collection[/i][/h3]
	At this early stage, we'll be keeping a close eye on player feedback
to identify and address bugs, balance issues, and other playability barriers.
After we determine that enough has been done to make the baseline experience smoother,
it will be time to begin adding new features and content variety.

[hr][/hr] 

[h1][b]Near-Future:[/b][/h1]
[h3][i]-World map visual overhaul[/i][/h3]
	At the moment, the world map is comprised of only a handful of shader-recolored tiles and some trees. Larger ground tiles with more variations will be used to fill the screen a bit more. The re-coloring shader is a bit slow, so this will be removed (using just normal pre-colored tiles) to help add performance overhead for other enhanced effects on the tiles or a larger map.
New vegetation and decorations will be placed to better convey the "otherworldly" vibe.
The background and edges of the map will also have a visual touch-up to feel more like a map and less like a strange empty board game.

[h3][i]-Item Storage[/i][/h3]
	Allow the player to manage and collect items on the world map screen. Decide what to take and what to leave for later!

[h3][i]-Characters[/i][/h3]
	New non-playable characters will appear to provide rewards, services, and/or activities. These characters will have a reputation value that can be increased through interaction, thus upgrading their services, providing better rewards, or assigning more difficult tasks.

[h3][i]-New Enemies[/i][/h3]
	The current single enemy type, called a "Jacklite" is a placeholder enemy that has existed since very early in development. 
This will be replaced by a similarly-behaving flying enemy with better art and animation. New enemies with their own sets of mutators will also be added.
Enemies are categorized by where they appear (All Areas/Forest-Only/etc.), and their relative size (small, medium, large).
Each species will have its own set of mixable abilities, much like the current Jacklite.
These abilities will be categorized in such a way that when any two enemies fuse, their mixed abilities will seem to be related to the parents even though only one species is chosen as a result. 
Example:
Enemy#1 is a small, weak flyer with a power-attack mutation.
Enemy#2 is a stronger, larger enemy with a dodge-move mutation. Enemy#2's species will be chosen as the result of fusion. It will inherit the dodge-move from its own species mutation pool, as well as a similar mutation categorized as a power-attack, but not the same exact one as Enemy#1's.

[h3][i]-New Items[/i][/h3]
	[b]Elixirs[/b] are meant to provide useful consumable effects, as well as enabling "weapon infusion". We will be expanding on the number of elixirs, as well as the effects they can put on weapons. An elixir of one type will have access to multiple related weapon infusion effects.
Example: Infusing a bomb elixir could get you splash damage on a weapon, or perhaps it could add other explosion-like effects that work differently.
This is because elixirs will likely have fewer consumable effect types than the number of possible weapon infusions we'd like to add, so they must be split among the elixirs based on which one seems most related to that elixir's theme. An elixir may apply a random infusion among those it has, but if an elixir is applied to a weapon with an existing matching infusion, it will be made more likely for that existing infusion effect to be enhanced rather than adding a new one of the same category.
	[b]Relics[/b] are items that provide a passive effect while held in the field inventory. They are comprised of two fused artifacts. Each artifact represents a general gameplay concept, and when two artifacts are fused, the resulting relic has an effect that relates or combines the two concepts in some way. 49 Relics have already been designed and sketched, forming from a total of 7 artifacts. Over time, these artifacts will be added to the game, expanding the pool of relics. It may be possible to expand beyond the planned 7 artifacts later.
	[b]Shrouded items[/b] are items that will be locked-off, hidden behind colorful smoke. Complete the task outlined by the shroud, and that item will be revealed, with a bonus added to it based on the type of shroud and/or type of item.

[h3][i]-New animations and improved effects[/i][/h3]
There are still placeholder graphics and incomplete or missing animations, once more of the game is established, we can start to touch these up.

[h3][i]-New tower biomes and decorations[/i][/h3]
New tower tilesets, floor-generation rules, objects, and gimmicks will be added to make each tower feel more alive and unique!

[hr][/hr] 

[h1][b]Later:[/b][/h1]
[h3][i]-Support for more languages[/i][/h3]
	Grabbus supports loading files for multiple languages, but needs more language-specific fonts and a way to switch between them. This can be done pretty easily, but we'll wait for when more text is in the game. In the meantime, the existing Spanish translation will continue to be maintained to make sure the system continues to work up until then.

[h3][i]-World map buildings and mechanics[/i][/h3]
	Build foundations to flatten land. Build roads, tunnels, and bridges to connect your buildings and explore further.
Rescue rats from towers! Build homes to house them, farms to feed them, resource extractors to supply them, and factories for them to help synthesize items. Micromanaging will be avoided. The idea is for you to set-and-forget most buildings, rather than having to manipulate or maintain them.
Rats will have their work speed and quality altered depending on how many rats there are, how much work is to be done, and how well their needs are met.
A hub area to handle interactions with major characters is also planned.

[h3][i]-Tower floor sub-objectives and mutators[/i][/h3]
	As the player climbs up the difficulty ranks, towers will spawn with alterations to their enemy composition, events, objectives, floor generation, obstacles, or otherwise. Towers that are left to sit for too many turns will begin to encroach on surrounding land by growing outward, developing more alterations over time, or even growing new floors. Towers will have an appearance that matches their tileset theme. 
	Objectives on some floors will require you to do something more complex than simply defeating all the enemies to proceed, especially requiring grabbing, fusing, manipulation, or throwing of whatever obstacles or gadgets are involved.

[h3][i]-Story missions and scenes[/i][/h3]
	Grabbus already has a partially-implemented cutscene editor. It is able to use expressive, lip-synced portraits and text to convey the story!
The current plan is for the story to be divided into somewhat self-contained chapters with their own subplot of characters and locations exploring some aspect of the world of Skixx. These chapters will tie into the overall narrative as they wrap-up, propelling our heroes further into the mystery...

notes.title: First patch!
notes.content:
[list]
[*] -On gamepad, default input for SHIELD/THROW has now been correctly set to Left Trigger as intended
[*] -Enemy damage-receiving radius extended slightly, making them a bit easier to hit
[*] -In gamepad mode, the world map cursor now starts properly centered
[*] -Projectiles now have a slightly larger minimum visual scale
[*] -More reliable handling of looped noises
[*] -Tower dungeon size is now drastically reduced to start, scaling up with dungeon potency(difficulty) and floor count
[*] -Random roll for number of total floors in a tower has been reworked
[*] -Loot rolls from rainbow seeds have been given drastically reduced scaling from difficulty
[*] -Number of treasure orbs on a floor is now affected by a random roll, there will be generally fewer as a result of this and reduced dungeon size
[*] -World potency(difficulty) now reduces by only 5% (multiplicative) instead of 10% on defeat, and now increases by one percent (additive) per cleared floor, in addition to the five percent per cleared tower (also additive)
[*] -Building costs have been drastically reduced (keep in mind: buildings are not very useful yet, an overhaul is planned here)
[/list]
